newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle seen steady-off, feeders steady-up.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle seen steady-off, feeders steady-up.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open steady to 0.100 cent lower while feeder cattle were called steady to 0.100 cent higher, analysts said.

Live cattle futures are expected to continue trending lower following the slipping cash cattle market. Cash cattle are seen trading at $63 per cwt this week and packers started out the week biding $62. Boxed beef values were also down in active trade as packers move out product, analysts said.
However, trade is epxected to light much of the week in futures ahead of Friday's Cattle-on-feed report, they said.

Early analyst projections put total onfeed cattle supplies in the major seven-state area between 112 and 114 percent of a year ago as of June 1. A number at the high end would be a record high. Placement estimates ranged from 110.5 to 124 percent and marketings 97.3 to 100 percent.

Feeder cattle futures were expected to uncover some early support after reaching 6-week lows. A gain in the lastest CME feeder cattle index and lower corn futures calls may provide support, analysts said.
However, the lower trend in cash fed cattle may keep the market under pressure, they added.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.28 at $77.76 per cwt, its highest level since August 19, 1994.
